questions.q: A TV tower has a height $72 \mathrm{~m}$. The maximum distance upto which TV transmission can be received is (Take, radius of the earth as $\left.6.4 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~m}\right)$
questions.solution:
The height of TV tower, $h=72 \mathrm{ m}$
The maximum distance upto which transmission can be received,
$d=\sqrt{2 R h}=\sqrt{2 \times 6.4 \times 10^6 \times 72}=30.35 \mathrm{ km}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A TV tower has a height $72 \mathrm{~m}$. The maximum distance upto which TV transmission can be received is (Take, radius of the earth as $\left.6.4 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~m}\right)$
questions.solution:
The maximum distance $d$ up to which the TV transmission can be received from a tower of height $h$ is given by the formula $d = \sqrt{2Rh}$, where $R$ is the radius of the Earth.

Given values are $h = 72 \text{ m}$ and $R = 6.4 \times 10^6 \text{ m}$.

Substituting these values into the formula:

$d = \sqrt{2 \times (6.4 \times 10^6 \text{ m}) \times 72 \text{ m}}$

$d = \sqrt{12.8 \times 10^6 \times 72}$

$d = \sqrt{921.6 \times 10^6}$

$d = \sqrt{921.6} \times 10^3 \text{ m}$

$d = 30.3578 \times 10^3 \text{ m}$

$d \approx 30.36 \text{ km}$.

Answer: 30.36 km

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Maximum amplitude of message signal in amplitude modulation is $20 \mathrm{ cm}$. If the amplitude of carrier wave is $40 \mathrm{ cm}$, then modulation index of modulated wave is
questions.solution:
The modulation index $\mu$ for an amplitude modulated wave is defined as the ratio of the amplitude of the message signal $A_m$ to the amplitude of the carrier wave $A_c$.

Given values are $A_m = 20 \text{ cm}$ and $A_c = 40 \text{ cm}$.

The formula for the modulation index is $\mu = \dfrac{A_m}{A_c}$.

Substituting the given values:

$\mu = \dfrac{20}{40} = 0.5$.

Answer: 0.5

questions.q: A TV tower is $120 \mathrm{ m}$ high. How much more height is to be added to it, if its coverage range is to become double?
questions.solution:
Initial height of TV tower, $h_{1}=120 \mathrm{ m}  Coverage range$ of TV tower is given as d=\sqrt{2 R h}$ where, $Ris radius of $the earth.  \begin{aligned}&\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d_{1}}{d_{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{h_{1}}{h_{2}}}\\
&\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d_{1}}{2 d_{1}}=\sqrt{\frac{120}{h_{2}}}\\
&\Rightarrow \quad \quad \frac{1}{4}=\frac{120}{h_{2}}\\
&\Rightarrow \quad h_{2}=480 \mathrm{ m}\\
&\left.\therefore \text{ Heighi to be added }=h_{2}-h_{1}=2 d_{1}\right] \\
&\quad=480-120=360 \mathrm{ m}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A message signal of frequency $10 \mathrm{kHz}$ and peak value of $10 \mathrm{ V}$ is used to moderate a carrier of frequency $1 \mathrm{MHz}$ and peak voltage $20 \mathrm{ V}$. The modulation index and side bands produced are
questions.solution:
Frequency of message signal, $f_{m}=10 \mathrm{kHz}$ 
Carrier frequency, $f_{c}=1 \mathrm{MHz}=1000 \mathrm{kHz}$
Peak value of message signal, $V_{m}=10 \mathrm{~V}$
Peak value of carrier signal, $V_{c}=20 \mathrm{~V}\therefore$ Modulation index, $\mu=\frac{V_{m}}{V_{c}}=\frac{10}{20}=0.5$
Upper side band frequency,

f_${\text{USB }}$=f_{c}+f_{m}=1000+10

=1010 $\mathrm{kHz}$Lower side band frequency,

$\begin{aligned}$f_${\text{LSB }}$ &=f_{c}-f_{m} \\
&=1000-10=990 $\mathrm{kHz}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The increase in the height of the tower of height $200 \mathrm{ m}$ to get its coverage range tripled is
questions.solution:
Given, height of the tower, $h_{1}=200 \mathrm{ m}$
If $R$ be the radius of the earth, then coverage range,
$d=\sqrt{2 R h} \Rightarrow d \propto \sqrt{h}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d_{1}}{d_{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{h_{1}}{h_{2}}}\begin{array}{ll}\text{ Since, } & d_{2}=3 d_{1} \\ \therefore & \frac{d_{1}}{3 d_{1}}=\sqrt{\frac{h_{1}}{h_{2}}}\end{array}
\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{3}=\sqrt{\frac{200}{h_{2}}}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{9}=\frac{200}{h_{2}}\Rightarrow \quad$ h_{2}=1800 $\mathrm{ m}\therefore Increase in the height of the tower
$=1800 $\mathrm{ m}-200 \mathrm{ m}=1600 \mathrm{ m}$
